items.title: feat: add --verbose flag to datalens clean command
items.body:
Closes #4

## What this PR does
Adds a `--verbose` flag to the `datalens clean` command that prints detailed information about the data cleaning pipeline operations. 

## Changes made
* **`datalens/cleaning.py`**: Updated `clean_data()` to accept a `verbose` boolean. When `True`, the function computes and returns a dictionary of metrics alongside the cleaned DataFrame (tracking duplicates removed, rows/columns handled for missing values, and coerced dtypes). The default `verbose=False` behavior is unchanged so all existing tests remain green.
* **`datalens/cli.py`**: Added the `@click.option` for `--verbose` to the `clean` command. If the user passes the flag, it unpacks the details dictionary and prints a formatted summary to the console.

## Acceptance criteria met
- [x] `datalens clean data.csv --verbose` prints extra details (duplicates, missing values handled, coerced dtypes).
- [x] Without `--verbose`, output is unchanged from current behavior.
- [x] The underlying logic for computing details lives entirely in `datalens/cleaning.py` (not inline in the CLI), preserving testability.
- [x] `pytest` passes locally.

items.title: [#3079] Fix: Add equals method to GravitinoVersion.java
items.body:
<!--
1. Title: [#<issue>] <type>(<scope>): <subject>
   Examples:
     - "[#123] feat(operator): support xxx"
     - "[#233] fix: check null before access result in xxx"
     - "[MINOR] refactor: fix typo in variable name"
     - "[MINOR] docs: fix typo in README"
     - "[#255] test: fix flaky test NameOfTheTest"
   Reference: https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/
2. If the PR is unfinished, please mark this PR as draft.
-->

### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR adds equals and hashCode methods to the GravitinoVersion class. These changes ensure that GravitinoVersion objects are compared consistently across different contexts, aligning with the natural ordering provided by the compareTo method.

### Why are the changes needed?

Without the equals method, comparing GravitinoVersion instances can lead to inconsistent behavior depending on whether compareTo or equals is used. This inconsistency can cause issues in collections that rely on equals and hashCode, such as HashMap and HashSet. Adding these methods ensures that GravitinoVersion instances are compared correctly and consistently, regardless of the method used.

Fix: #3079 

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No, this PR does not introduce any user-facing changes.

### How was this patch tested?

Basic testing was performed by adding unit tests to verify that the equals and hashCode methods function correctly and consistently. These tests ensure that GravitinoVersion objects with identical version strings are equal and have the same hash code, and that the compareTo method maintains consistent ordering.
